say: Your first cream, your batch formula, and a facial oil.
This is the video for module two of Natural Skincare.
First you will make an oil-in-water cream. The method is the same for 100 g or 5 kg.

panel.rule: Preservative goes in at about 45°C, below its maximum temperature.

say: For example, Chioma in Owerri makes a 200 g practice cream. Her water jug with the water phase weighs 412.40 g.
At 75 degrees she starts a 20-minute timer, and keeps it between 73 and 77.
Afterwards the jug weighs 405.10 g, so she adds 7.30 g of hot distilled water. Without that, her cream would be about 7 g short of water.
After several blend-cool-blend rounds, at 44 degrees she adds 1.00 g of preservative. Her cream is smooth and white, and she uses it herself only.
Write recipes in percentages, so any batch size comes out the same. For example, Rukayat in Ilorin wants five 50 g jars. That is a 250 g batch.
Her learning formula has 70.5 percent distilled water. 250 times 70.5 divided by 100 is 176.25 g.
Emulsifying wax at 6 percent is 15.00 g.
The preservative at 0.5 percent is 1.25 g. That is why you need a 0.01 g scale. Always weigh, never measure by spoon or cup.
Every line adds up to 250.00 g. Some cream always stays on the jug, so add a 5 to 10 percent allowance.
Too much preservative can irritate skin, and too little leaves it under-protected. Stay inside the published range.

panel.heading: Grams = batch × percent ÷ 100
panel.rule: Never raise the preservative 'to be safe'. Stay in its range.

say: A facial oil has no water, so no preservative. A water-based serum, with aloe or a hydrosol, needs one like any cream.
The risk for oils is rancidity: a sharp smell like crayon or paint. Build most of the blend on a stable, light base such as jojoba.

panel.heading: Keep your oil fresh
items: Delicate oils like rosehip in smaller amounts
Amber or blue glass, filled near the top

say: For example, Efe in Benin City uses jojoba 50 percent, baobab 30 percent, rosehip 19.5 percent, and vitamin E 0.5 percent. Oils weigh roughly 0.9 g per ml, so a 30 ml bottle needs 27 g.

say: Vitamin E slows rancidity, but it is not a preservative.

say: Fill amber or cobalt blue glass close to the top, and store it away from sunlight. Leave essential oils out of your first face oil, because some, like bergamot, can make skin react to sunlight.

say: Jugs at 75 degrees are hot enough to burn. Lift them with oven gloves, pour slowly onto a stable surface, and keep the blender cable away from the water bath.

cards.d: Jugs at 75°C burn. Use oven gloves, pour slowly onto a stable surface, keep the cable away.
Sanitise with 70% alcohol and let it dry fully. Any drop left inside ends up in the oil.
Use practice creams yourself. Do not give or sell any cream before the Module 3 checks.

say: No water does not mean no hygiene. Sanitise with 70 percent alcohol, and let everything dry completely.

say: To remember. Heat to about 75 degrees and hold the water 20 minutes. Top up lost water by weight. Add the preservative at about 45.
Grams equal batch size times percent divided by 100. And for oils, use a stable base, vitamin E and dark glass.
